name: Pride Kickoff: HHHH x Twisted Arts x Tulsa Artist Fellowship
venue: Tulsa Artist Fellowship, 109 MLK Jr Blvd, Tulsa, OK
description: Cancel your plans to do nothing, baby. The Tulsa Artist Fellowship First Friday goes full Pride with Homo Hotel Happy Hour and Twisted Arts, drag at 8, and a fat zero-dollar cover.
website_description: Sweetheart, this is not the night to stay home. The Tulsa Artist Fellowship First Friday becomes a full-blown Pride kickoff, with Homo Hotel Happy Hour and Twisted Arts joining the Fellowship for the very first time. Avery Marshall, a Black trans queer Tulsa artist, sings live at 7, a nine-queen drag show follows at 8, and a charity raffle runs all night for Queer Lit Collective's second birthday. Open studios, fresh art, music, and drag, all stitched into one downtown night, and it is completely free. Best-time tip for the shy ones: roll in around the 5 o'clock happy hour, start at the far end of the studios to beat the crowd, then post up near the stage before the queens come out.
source_note: W23 EOTW #1. First-ever HHHH x Twisted Arts collab, Tulsa Pride kickoff. Details from project_hhhh_pride_kickoff memory (2026-05-13). Added 2026-06-01.

name: Council Oak Men's Chorale: Jukebox - Songs You Know & Love
description: A gay men's chorus going OFF on the songs you already love, from Sister Act to Disney to the pop you scream in the car. Coolest singalong in town, two nights only.
website_description: Forget whatever you pictured when you heard the words men's chorale, because Council Oak goes THERE. Jukebox: Songs You Know and Love is a full gay men's chorus tearing into the songs you already know every word to, from Sister Act to Disney to the pop anthems you scream in the car, all big harmonies and zero stuffiness. It is loud, it is a little camp, it is genuinely cool, and it hands you chills you did not sign up for. Tickets at counciloak.org. Best-time tip: buy ahead, sit a few rows back so the whole wall of sound hits you at once, and do not act surprised when a song you know by heart still gets you.
source_note: W23 EOTW. Jukebox concert June 5 & 6 (from counciloak.org poster). Cool gay-mens-chorus pop vibe; do NOT name a setlist (Whitney is NOT performing).

name: Monday Movie Night at the Tulsa Eagle
venue: Tulsa Eagle, 1338 E 3rd St, Tulsa, OK
description: Queer movie night at the Eagle with $5 wells all day, tonight it's 'I Love You Phillip Morris' (yes, the gay Jim Carrey con-man romp). Low-key, comfy, and gay as it gets.
website_description: The Tulsa Eagle kicks the week off soft and gay with Monday Movie Night, and tonight Circle Cinema sponsors a screening of 'I Love You Phillip Morris,' the gloriously unhinged Jim Carrey prison-romance caper. Isaac opens at 2 with $5 well cocktails all day, so you can ease in before the 7pm showtime. It is the kind of easy, no-pressure Monday that's perfect if you want company without a whole production. Best-time tip: roll in a little before 7, grab a $5 well, and post up where you can see the screen, this is a sit-back-and-laugh kind of night.

name: Gaymer Night at the Tulsa Eagle
venue: Tulsa Eagle, 1338 E 3rd St, Tulsa, OK
description: Gaymer Night at the Eagle with Kay Kay, where the controllers come out and so does your competitive streak. Show up at 8 and let the games (and the trash talk) begin.
website_description: Right after the movie, Kay Kay runs Gaymer Night at the Tulsa Eagle starting at 8, a laid-back hang for queer folks who'd rather bond over a controller than a dance floor. Expect games, friendly trash talk, and an easy in if you're shy, because nothing breaks the ice like co-op chaos. It runs all night, so there's no rush. Best-time tip: get there around 8, tell Kay Kay you're new, and let someone hand you a controller, you'll have three new friends by the second round.

name: Highly Suspect in Concert
venue: The Tulsa Theater, 105 W Reconciliation Way, Tulsa, OK
description: Gritty alt-rock takes over the historic Tulsa Theater, the kind of loud, sweaty show that knocks a Tuesday loose. Grab a ticket and go feel something.
website_description: Highly Suspect brings their gritty, brooding alt-rock to the gorgeous old Tulsa Theater, and it is exactly the jolt a random Tuesday needs. Big riffs, big feelings, and a crowd that came to let loose under that historic ceiling. If you have been meaning to get out more, a loud show in a beautiful room is a painless way to start. Best-time tip: get there in time for the opener, find a spot on the floor near the bar, and let the wall of sound do the rest.

name: Open Mic Night at Gypsy Coffee House
venue: Gypsy Coffee House, 303 M.L.K. Jr Blvd, Tulsa, OK
description: Open mic at Gypsy, where the coffee's strong and the talent is gloriously unpredictable. Slip in around 6:30, clap loud, and maybe even put your name down.
website_description: Gypsy Coffee House throws open the mic on Tuesday nights, and it is the warm, low-stakes, anything-can-happen kind of room that artsy queer folks love. Expect poets, musicians, and the occasional gloriously chaotic first-timer, all in a cozy downtown coffeehouse with real character. No cover, no pressure, just a good seat and a strong drink. Best-time tip: get there by 6:30 to grab a comfy spot, order something warm, and clap like you mean it, the performers feed off a kind room.

name: Goff Fest: Annual Pride Celebration
venue: Tulsa Artist Fellowship Studios, 109 MLK Jr. Blvd E, Tulsa, OK 74103
description: Goff Fest throws its Annual Pride Celebration at the TFA Studios, honoring Tulsa's gay-architect legacy with art, community, and a fat zero-dollar cover. Free admission, all welcome.
website_description: Goff Fest celebrates the legacy of Bruce Goff, the gloriously unconventional gay architect who left his fingerprints all over Oklahoma, and the Annual Pride Celebration is its big queer night out. Held at the Tulsa Artist Fellowship Studios, it folds art, design, and community into one warm First-Friday Pride kickoff, and it is completely free. Best-time tip: come a little after 6 while the light is still good in the studios, wander the work, then settle in as the crowd warms up.
source_note: Added 2026-06-05 per William. Goff Center (@goff_fest) added as a standing source this session.

name: Bruce Goff's Birthday Bash
venue: Tulsa Spotlight Theater, 1381 Riverside Drive, Tulsa, OK
description: Goff Fest closes out with Bruce Goff's Birthday Bash at the Spotlight Theater, the wonderfully weird building he designed himself. Free to get in, drinks and snacks for sale, six hours of celebrating a queer Tulsa legend.
website_description: Goff Fest wraps with a birthday party for Bruce Goff at the Tulsa Spotlight Theater, the riverside building Goff himself designed and one of the most charmingly offbeat spaces in town. Expect a relaxed, all-day hang celebrating the openly gay architect's legacy, with drinks and snacks available and admission completely free. Best-time tip: drift in early afternoon when the river light hits the building, take the architecture in, then stay for the party energy as the afternoon rolls on.
source_note: Added 2026-06-05 per William (IG post @goff_fest DZFWPFxkW7c). Goff Center added as a standing source this session.

name: Melanin Pride Yoga in the Park
description: Celebrate Pride in flow with KLASSIC's Melanin Pride Yoga in the Park, a Black queer outdoor session in the summer sun. Bring your own mat, they handle the water and snacks. Text or DM INFO to 918-888-6842 for the spot.
website_description: KLASSIC brings Black queer Tulsa a gorgeous way to mark Pride with Melanin Pride Yoga in the Park, an open-air flow built around community, melanin, and joy. Bring a mat and an open heart; water and snacks are provided, and the exact park location comes when you text or DM INFO to 918-888-6842. Best-time tip: message ahead for the location, arrive a few minutes early to claim a soft patch of grass, and let a morning of breath and sunshine set the tone for your whole weekend.
source_note: Added 2026-06-05 per William (IG @upflykai post DZNfphtss4k). KLASSIC added as a standing source this session.

name: The Pride Era Drag Bingo
description: Oklahomans for Equality presents The Pride Era Drag Bingo with Porsche Lynn, Shanel Sterling, and Iman Scott. Doors at 2, show at 3, dab those cards and let the queens run the room. 18+ with ID.
website_description: Oklahomans for Equality turns bingo into a full drag spectacle with The Pride Era Drag Bingo at Bricktown Comedy Club, hosted by Porsche Lynn with Shanel Sterling and Iman Scott bringing the looks and the laughs. Doors open at 2 with the show at 3, and yes, you can actually win while the queens work the room. It is 18+ with valid ID, with premium front-row and general admission seating, and showroom guests grab at least two food or drink items. Best-time tip: buy online before prices jump at the door, get there near doors at 2 to snag a good table, and keep a dauber in each hand because these rounds move fast.
source_note: Added 2026-06-05 per William (OKEQ FB event share 1E3n7Ggp4p). OKEQ already a standing source.

name: PINT's Rockin' Auction Extravaganza
venue: Venue Shrine, 112 E 18th St S, Tulsa, OK 74119
description: Rock for Rescues, baby. Cobi Lalas plays the 70s through 90s sing-alongs you know by heart, there's a silent auction packed with art and oddities, and every dollar sends a homeless pup toward a real home. Tickets on StubWire.
website_description: Paws In Need Tulsa throws its Rockin' Auction Extravaganza at Venue Shrine, and it is the rare fundraiser that actually slaps. Local rockers Cobi Lalas open with the rock classics from the 70s, 80s, and 90s you will absolutely sing along to, then swing into their own quantum groove rock, all grunge grit and red-dirt soul. While the music plays you can wander a silent auction stacked with artwork, collectibles, experiences, and musical instruments, and every ticket and every winning bid funds PINT's transport program that drives homeless animals to rescue partners across the country. It runs 3 to 7pm, all heart, all good cause. Tickets are on StubWire. Best-time tip for the shy ones: come right at 3 while the auction tables are fresh and the room is still easy to work, scope your bids early, then settle in for the second set when the band gets weird and wonderful.
source_note: Added 2026-06-05 per William. Verified live from the @PINT.inc FB event (id 1725078808494256, created same day) via personal Chrome; @PawsInNeedAuction online item-auction bidding also closes Jul 19 2026 6:30pm. It is the kind of low-key, browse-and-chat event that is easy to walk into solo. Best-time tip: come around opening at noon while the tables are full, take a slow loop, and chat up the makers, queer artists love to talk about their work.

name: Tulsa Pride Festival & Parade
venue: Tulsa Arts District / Pride Street, downtown Tulsa
description: The big one. Oklahomans for Equality's Tulsa Pride parade and festival takes over downtown, drag, vendors, music, and the whole community out loud.
website_description: Tulsa Pride is the main event, Oklahomans for Equality's flagship parade and festival that fills downtown's Tulsa Arts District with floats, drag, vendors, food, and the entire community out and proud. Note that OKEQ moved the big Pride to the second Saturday of October, so this, not June, is Tulsa's marquee Pride. Best-time tip: stake out a parade spot early, then flow into the festival, wear sunscreen and comfortable shoes, and pace yourself because this one goes all day.

name: Re-Elect Laura Bellis: Pride-Season Celebration (Tulsa City Council, District 4)
description: City Councilor Laura Bellis throws a Pride-season party to keep District 4 in pro-equality hands, backed by a whole roster of community co-hosts. Suggested 27 dollars, a nod to the 27th anniversary of Tulsa's first Pride parade. RSVP for the address.
website_description: Laura Bellis is the kind of local leader who actually shows up for queer Tulsa, and this Pride-season celebration is your invitation to help keep her on the Tulsa City Council representing District Four. It is a warm, easy room full of community co-hosts, all there to support candidates committed to protecting human rights for every Tulsan. The suggested minimum donation is a sweet 27 dollars, honoring the 27th anniversary of Tulsa's first Pride parade, and the location is shared once you RSVP through the ActBlue link. Best-time tip for the shy ones: RSVP early so you get the address, then roll in right at 6 while the crowd is still small and easy to work, introduce yourself to one of the co-hosts, and you will have three new friends before the speeches even start. Showing up for an ally like this is one of the most useful nights you can give the community.
source_note: Added 2026-06-06 per William (flyer he sent). Laura Bellis re-election special event, Thu Jun 11 2026, 6-7:30pm, location upon RSVP. name: Rainbow Harvest: Free Farmers Market
venue: Dennis R. Neill Equality Center, 621 E 4th St
description: Free produce, zero judgment, and a whole lot of queer neighbors filling their tote bags at the Equality Center. Roll in between 1 and 4, grab what you need, and stay for the company. Pre-register so they know to expect you.
website_description: Rainbow Harvest is the Equality Center's free farmers market, and it is exactly the kind of low-key, big-hearted Saturday a shy introvert can actually handle. No cover, no pressure, just fresh groceries handed out from 1 to 4 PM and a crowd of LGBTQIA+ folks and allies who genuinely want you there. Pre-register at the form so the volunteers can pack enough for everyone, then show up, fill a bag, and let yourself be part of the neighborhood. Best-time tip: come right at 1 when the produce is fullest and the line is shortest, say hi to a volunteer, and you will leave with groceries and probably a new face you recognize next week.
source_note: OKEQ event-calendar scrape (Sunday W24 staging, 2026-06-07). Weekly free market at the Equality Center; re-verify on okeq.org/event-calendar before each week.

name: Queer Crafters Club
venue: Dennis R. Neill Equality Center, 621 E 4th St
description: Bring your half-finished cross-stitch, your glue gun, or absolutely nothing but yourself. Queer Crafters Club is two hours of making things and making friends, Thursday night at the Equality Center. Beginners and total chaos-crafters equally welcome.
website_description: Queer Crafters Club is the gentlest possible excuse to leave the house on a Thursday. From 6 to 8 PM at the Dennis R. Neill Equality Center, LGBTQIA+ crafters of every skill level gather to knit, paint, bead, glue, and gossip. You do not need to be good at anything, and you do not even need to bring a project, there is usually a spare set of supplies and a spare seat at the table. Best-time tip: walk in around 6 when folks are still setting up, claim a chair next to whoever looks friendliest, and let the small talk happen over a craft instead of forced eye contact. It recurs most Thursdays, so if this one sneaks up on you, there is always next week.
source_note: OKEQ event-calendar scrape (Sunday W24 staging, 2026-06-07). Weekly recurring Thu at the Equality Center; candidate to promote to a recurring source later.

name: Noche Latina: Latin Night at the Tulsa Eagle
venue: Tulsa Eagle, 1338 E 3rd St, Tulsa, OK
description: La rumba mas hot de Tulsa lands at the Eagle. DJ Bleiz spins reggaeton, dembow, y mas, with drink specials all night. 10pm en adelante, no te lo pierdas.
website_description: The Tulsa Eagle turns up the heat with Noche Latina, the bar's Latin Night and easily the hottest rumba in town. Live DJ Bleiz runs the booth all night with reggaeton, dembow, and more, there are drink specials to keep you moving, and the floor stays open from 10pm onward. It is a loud, joyful, everyone-welcome night to dance off the week. Best-time tip for the shy ones: get there a little after 10 while the floor is filling in, grab one of the drink specials, and let the first reggaeton track do the rest, nobody at the Eagle is watching how you dance.
source_note: Added 2026-06-15 per William (event flyer he sent). Tulsa Eagle Latin Night, Fri Jun 19 2026, 10pm onward, 1338 E 3rd St. Live DJ Bleiz; reggaeton/dembow; drink specials. venue: DVL Club & Lounge, 302 S Frankfort Ave, Tulsa, OK (Blue Dome District)
description: DVL throws open the Blue Dome doors for an LGBTQ+ social, the woman-owned queer spot where the cocktails are themed and the dance floor finds you. Roll in after work and let the night build around you.
website_description: DVL Club & Lounge, the woman-owned LGBTQ+ bar in Tulsa's Blue Dome District, hosts an LGBTQ+ social this Thursday, the easy come-as-you-are queer night out that asks nothing of you but showing up. Themed drinks, a friendly room, and a back space made for dancing. Doors open at 4 with happy hour running until 10, so you can ease in early before the crowd lands. Best-time tip for the shy ones: come during happy hour while the room is still mellow, post up at the bar where the bartenders will chat you up, and you will have found your people by the time the music gets loud.

name: Pride Anthem Drag Sing-Along at Elote
venue: Elote Cafe & Catering, 514 S Boston Ave, Tulsa, OK
description: Grab the mic and let it RIP, honey. Karma Eclectic hosts a Pride anthem drag sing-along at Elote, all glitter, camp, and pure queer joy. Belt the diva number you scream in the car and let the room carry you.
website_description: Elote turns its dining room into a karaoke cathedral for the Pride Anthem Drag Sing-Along, hosted by the one and only Karma Eclectic. Think every gay anthem you know by heart, dramatic lip syncs, real vocal moments, and a room full of people who genuinely want you to grab the mic. It runs 6 to 8 on Saturday night, it is glitter and camp and zero judgment, and tickets are on Eventbrite. Best-time tip for the shy ones: get there right at 6 while the song list is wide open, put your name down before the nerves talk you out of it, and pick the anthem you already know every word to, this crowd will sing the bridge right along with you.

name: Great Plains Rodeo (Oklahoma Gay Rodeo)
venue: Oklahoma City (Great Plains Rodeo Association, IGRA)
description: Boots, buckles, and a whole lot of queer cowboy energy. The Great Plains Rodeo is Oklahoma's IGRA-sanctioned gay rodeo, three days of real rodeo, camp, and community. Road-trip worthy, darling.
website_description: The Great Plains Rodeo is Oklahoma's gay rodeo, sanctioned by the International Gay Rodeo Association, and it is exactly the gloriously specific queer Americana you did not know you needed. Three days of barrel racing, bull riding, drag, dancing, and the friendliest boots-and-buckles crowd in the region, all in Oklahoma City the weekend of August 7 to 9. It is an easy road trip from Tulsa and worth every mile. Best-time tip for the shy ones: go for the Saturday daytime events when the grandstand is relaxed and folks love to explain what is happening, then stay for the evening social where the real community magic happens.
source_note: Added 2026-06-18 (scraper repair campaign). Great Plains Rodeo Association, IGRA-sanctioned Oklahoma gay rodeo, weekend of Aug 7-9 2026 in OKC (confirmed via greatplainsrodeo.org weekend schedule). venue: The Campbell Hotel, 2636 E 11th St, Tulsa, OK
description: First Friday on Historic Route 66. The Campbell is the restored 1927 Spanish Colonial — the very first full-service hotel on Route 66 in Tulsa. Free admission, charity raffle all night.

name: Monthly Clothing Swap at YBR
description: YBR's monthly clothing swap is tonight at 6, honey: bring what you never wear, leave with someone else's treasure. Free Piehole pizza at 7 while it lasts, so come early and work the racks first.
website_description: Yellow Brick Road's monthly clothing swap runs tonight from 6, and it is the easiest possible way to walk into Tulsa's only lesbian bar for the first time: everyone has a built-in reason to talk to you (that jacket, where did you get that jacket). Bring a bag of clothes you never wear, trade for someone else's castoffs, and stay for free Piehole pizza at 7 while supplies last. Come solo, browse the racks at your own speed, and remember the cave welcomes the whole community, not just the girls. Details on Instagram @tulsaybr.
source_note: Tip via DM IG captured 2026-07-06 09:40; reviewed before publish

name: PFLAG Tulsa Monthly Meeting
venue: Youth Services of Tulsa, 311 S Madison Ave
description: PFLAG Tulsa's monthly meeting: parents, families, and allies of 2SLGBTQIA+ Tulsans, first Saturday at 7. Come as you are, share only if you want to, and leave with people in your corner.
website_description: PFLAG Tulsa meets the first Saturday of every month at 7 p.m. at Youth Services of Tulsa. It is everyday people: parents whose kid just came out, family members with questions, allies who want to do right by the people they love. Meetings open with introductions if you are comfortable, and what is shared in the room stays in the room. If your family is figuring things out, this is the softest landing in Tulsa. No cost, no pressure, no judgment. More at tulsapflag.org.

name: HHHH First Friday: PFLAG Tulsa Fundraiser
description: Homo Hotel Happy Hour takes over the Courtyard Downtown, and this month every dollar raised goes to PFLAG Tulsa. Come for the hotel-bar glamour, stay because your cover charge keeps parents showing up for their queer kids.
website_description: August's Homo Hotel Happy Hour lands at the Courtyard Downtown on Boston Ave, 6 to 8 p.m., and it is a fundraiser for PFLAG Tulsa, the folks who have been showing up for 2SLGBTQIA+ Tulsans and their families every month for years. First Fridays at HHHH are the easiest social on the calendar: a hotel bar full of friendly faces, no dress code, no agenda, come alone and you will not stay alone long. This one comes with a bonus: the money goes somewhere that matters.

name: Drag Bingo
description: Sunday afternoon drag bingo with Porsche Lynn in full glam, five free cards, and a whole room hollering BINGO louder than the emcee. Slip in at doors (2pm) for a booth near the stage, sugar, and let the daubers do your socializing for you.
website_description: Bricktown Comedy Club Tulsa turns Sunday afternoon into a glitter-drenched bingo hall with Porsche Lynn working the mic in looks that could stop traffic on Yale. Your $15 gets you five free cards for five games, real prizes on the line, and the kind of crowd that treats a stranger like an old friend by the second round. It is an 18-and-up afternoon show with a two-item food-and-drink minimum, so order the nachos and settle in. Introverts, this one is built for you: the game gives your hands something to do, the daubing gives you cover, and nobody expects a speech, just a shriek of BINGO when your card fills. Doors at 2, show at 3, at 5982 S Yale Ave. Come at doors to claim a booth near the stage with a clean sightline and an easy path out, then let Porsche do the heavy lifting.
source_note: Bricktown Comedy Club Tulsa recurring Drag Bingo (host Porsche Lynn, Sun 3pm, 18+, $15/5 cards). Added 2026-07-09 per William (venue keeps comping tickets; promote them). Live-verified on bricktowntulsa.com/events + show page 374468. Also captured durably via rendered_site_specs json_ld spce; this manual entry gives the featured-quality card for W28.

name: Two Spirit Celebration: Stomp Dance
venue: Cherokee Nation Powwow Grounds (next to), Tahlequah, OK
description: The Two Spirit Celebration opens Friday night with a Stomp Dance beside the Cherokee Nation Powwow Grounds, honoring Native queer folks the old way, under the stars, feet to the ground, everybody welcome. Alcohol and drug free. Come as you are, sugar.
website_description: The Intercultural Partnership Council kicks off its Two Spirit Celebration with a Friday-night Stomp Dance right beside the Cherokee Nation Powwow Grounds in Tahlequah, 6 to 10 PM. This is Two-Spirit tradition held with pride: Native LGBTQ folks and the whole community moving together in the circle, the shell-shakers keeping time, everyone welcome no matter where you come from. It is completely alcohol and drug free, and there is no charge for food or activities. Best-time tip for the shy ones: get there right at 6 while the light is still soft and folks are gathering, stand at the edge of the circle to watch and listen first, and when you feel ready, someone will wave you in, that is exactly how the dance is meant to work. General info at tinyurl.com/ipctahlequah.
source_note: Added 2026-07-10 per William (flyer from All Nations Two-Spirit Society, posted Jun 5). Two Spirit Celebration Oct 23-24 2026, a project of the Intercultural Partnership Council. Partners: Cherokee Nation, Tahlequah Public Library, All Nations Two Spirit Society, Squirrel Ridge Ceremonial Grounds. Everyone welcome, all events alcohol/drug free, no charge for food or activities. General info ipc.gadugi@gmail.com / tinyurl.com/ipctahlequah. Tahlequah is ~65mi SE of Tulsa but OK-wide marquee Two-Spirit event, priority 1.

name: Two Spirit Celebration: Symposium
description: Saturday morning the Two Spirit Celebration heads to the Tahlequah Public Library for a symposium, honest talk about Two-Spirit history, identity, and community, coffee-warm and everyone welcome. Free, alcohol and drug free.
website_description: The middle chapter of the Two Spirit Celebration is a Saturday-morning symposium at the Tahlequah Public Library, 8:30 AM to 12:30 PM. This is the learning heart of the weekend: Two-Spirit history, culture, and lived experience shared out loud in a warm, welcoming room, open to Native and non-Native folks alike. It is free, alcohol and drug free, and there is no charge for food or activities. Best-time tip for the shy ones: a library is the gentlest possible place to walk into something new, so come near the 8:30 start, grab a seat toward the back, and let yourself just listen, nobody is going to put you on the spot. General info at tinyurl.com/ipctahlequah.
source_note: Added 2026-07-10 per William (flyer from All Nations Two-Spirit Society). Day 2 morning session of the Two Spirit Celebration. See Stomp Dance entry for full partner/contact detail.

name: Two Spirit Celebration: Community Powwow
venue: Cherokee Nation Powwow Arena, Tahlequah, OK
description: The Two Spirit Celebration closes big Saturday evening with a Community Powwow at the Cherokee Nation Powwow Arena, regalia, drum, and the whole circle out proud. Everyone welcome, alcohol and drug free, no charge to be there, darling.
website_description: The Two Spirit Celebration goes out on a high note with a Community Powwow at the Cherokee Nation Powwow Arena in Tahlequah, 4 to 10 PM Saturday. Six hours of drum, dance, and regalia, a Two-Spirit-honoring gathering with the whole community invited into the circle. It is alcohol and drug free with no charge for food or activities, so you can stay as long as your heart wants. Best-time tip for the shy ones: arrive around 4 while the arena is still filling and find a spot on the bleachers to take it all in, watch a round or two to learn the rhythm, and stand when they call an intertribal, that is the dance where everyone, spectators included, is welcome to step in. General info at tinyurl.com/ipctahlequah.
source_note: Added 2026-07-10 per William (flyer from All Nations Two-Spirit Society). Day 2 evening finale of the Two Spirit Celebration. See Stomp Dance entry for full partner/contact detail.

website_description: The usual Babes and Bi-cons dance floor, except it is Val's birthday and the bar is making a night of it. Drink feature, a raffle, and SuperGay vodka on special.
